name: Sort the shared inbox and draft replies
summary: Sorts the shared inbox into work orders, quote requests, complaints, questions, noise and other, drafts template replies, and assigns each thread with a turnaround reminder. Crons read, draft and label; a person approves every reply before it is sent.

all.evidence: 10 discovery calls describe this way of triaging the inbox

covered_by.message-arrives: intake (polls every 10 minutes; no webhook yet)

crons.name: intake
crons.summary: New mail from the shared inbox and the shared mailbox, sorted by keyword rules.

crons.name: draft
crons.summary: Queue approved template replies for approval. Mail with no template is left for a person.

crons.name: assign
crons.summary: Assign each new thread to the teammate in Front, or label it in Gmail, with a turnaround reminder.

draft_ops_note: Draft operations reach nobody outside the business: reads, an assignee or reminder inside Front, a Gmail label, a Gmail draft. Sending a reply is a live operation and waits for a person.

front.covers: shared inbox: read open unassigned conversations, assign, reminder, template reply after approval

google-workspace.covers: Gmail: read unread inbox threads, label, draft reply, send the draft after approval

gaps: Microsoft 365 (Outlook): no adapter here. The kit maps the mailbox calls, but the mining file says no user-mailbox operation is mapped for reading, moving or replying; check that before building one.
WhatsApp, ConnectWise, OnRent, Sling and Asana: named in the calls, not mapped as triage steps. Follow-up by WhatsApp and the record-keeping copies stay with the owner.
Front approval sends the template text as a new reply. It does not send a Front draft, so an edit made in Front does not change what is sent. Gmail approval sends the draft itself.
Front and Google Workspace are docs-only until a live account proves the reads and writes. Front's help pages describe the inbox but not its reply, assign or reminder screens.
Intake polls every 10 minutes. There is no webhook, so a message can wait up to 10 minutes before it is sorted.

Mail older than lookback_hours (default 24) is not triaged, assigned or answered. Reply approvals are capped at per_run_limit (default 20) a run. A thread whose reply cannot be queued (for example, a sender with no valid address) is parked with reply_error: a person answers it, and it stays in the assign run. A reply that fails to queue for a temporary reason is parked too, so it needs a person to answer rather than a retry.
The four-hour target is a wall-clock reminder, not a business-hours calculation.
Triage calls and calendar booking are judgment work for the agent skill. Nothing here books a call.
Close-out (resolve or archive) is not built. Both platforms can do it, but a person does it for now.

evidence.calls: 77 calls in the worklist; 19 read in detail, 10 of them describe the process step by step
evidence.platforms: Front, Google Workspace and Microsoft 365 help pages, mapped by step; Front and Google Workspace have the most steps with support
